1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust upward bias by 2–5% for the first 5–10 days.

2. Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.68 → 81.20+), then corrects — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% after a spike > 10% above prior 30-day mean.

3. Late forecast days (days 25–30) show underestimation — increase forecast by 1–3% for days 25–30 to align with mean reversion toward recent true values.

4. Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — if true price drops below 75.00, forecast should adjust downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.

5. Forecast mean is typically 2–4% higher than true mean — apply a global downward correction of 2–4% to all forecast values to reduce systematic overfitting.
